title: The Poems of Alexander Pope, Twickenham Edition (11 volumes)
reliability_notes: The standard scholarly edition of Pope's poetical works, volume by volume, with collated early texts and full editorial introductions; publication ran from 1938 to 1969.

title: Jonathan Swift: Critical, Scholastic, and Variorum Edition
reliability_notes: The variorum scholarly edition of Swift's prose and verse begun in 1967; its separate volumes carry the collated texts and the history of the printing of Gulliver's Travels and the tract.

title: The Spectator, 4 volumes
reliability_notes: The definitive text of the original Spectator papers with attribution of authorship, notes and index; the basis for all quotation from the 1711-12 and 1714 series.

title: The Yale Edition of the Works of Samuel Johnson (21 volumes)
author_or_editor: W. Jackson Bate and James L. Clifford (general editors)
reliability_notes: The collected scholarly edition of Johnson's poems, tales, periodical papers, criticism and letters; publication began in 1958 and continued to 2001.

title: The Life of Samuel Johnson, 6 volumes (Birkbeck Hill edition)
reliability_notes: The long-standard annotated text of Boswell's Life, revised by L. F. Powell in 1934-64; the ordinary reference text for Boswell.

title: The Poems of Thomas Gray, William Collins and Oliver Goldsmith
reliability_notes: A scholarly English-text edition with variant readings and commentary, standard for the middle-century school; publication details from the Longman series list.

title: The Poems of Robert Burns, 3 volumes
reliability_notes: The variorum text of Burns's poems with Scots glossary and commentary; the reference edition for the Kilmarnock and Edinburgh printings.

title: The Norton Anthology of English Literature, 10th edition, Volume D: The Romantic Period
reliability_notes: The standard teaching anthology; its opening section carries the late-eighteenth-century writers (Burns, Cowper, Blake, Wollstonecraft, the Gothic novelists) used at the close of this installment.

title: The Cambridge Companion to Eighteenth-Century Poetry
reliability_notes: Essays on the Augustan, sentimental, graveyard and preromantic poetic modes, on versification and on the verse of the periodical press.

title: The Cambridge Companion to the Eighteenth-Century Novel
reliability_notes: Survey essays on the forms, readers and institutions of eighteenth-century prose fiction.

title: The Cambridge Companion to Alexander Pope
reliability_notes: Essays on Pope's life, the Augustan satire, the translation of Homer and the poetry of the country seat.

title: The Cambridge Companion to Samuel Johnson
reliability_notes: Essays on Johnson's moral and religious thought, criticism, lexicography and periodical writing.

title: The Cambridge Companion to Gothic Fiction
reliability_notes: Essays tracing the origins and history of the Gothic mode, including its eighteenth-century foundations.

title: The Rise of the Novel: Studies in Defoe, Richardson and Fielding
reliability_notes: The influential critical history that framed the discussion of 'formal realism' and the empirical philosophy behind early-eighteenth-century fiction.

title: The Novel: An Anthology of Criticism and Practice, 1700-1800
reliability_notes: Assembled prefaces, advertisements, critical essays and extracts documenting eighteenth-century debate about prose fiction.

title: An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, 2 volumes
reliability_notes: The long-standard text of the 1776 edition, reprinted by the University of Chicago Press in 1976; the Glasgow edition has since superseded it for scholarly citation.

title: The Theory of Moral Sentiments (Cambridge Texts in the History of Philosophy)
reliability_notes: A critical text of Adam Smith's 1759 theory of sympathy and the impartial spectator, with editorial introduction and notes.

title: A Treatise of Human Nature (Clarendon Edition of the Works of David Hume)
author_or_editor: David Fate Norton and Mary J. Norton (eds.)
reliability_notes: The scholarly text of the 1739-40 Treatise with variants from the 1742 Advertisement and the later editions.

title: The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano
reliability_notes: A critical reprint of the 1789 narrative with introduction, notes and documentary apparatus; Carretta's scholarship also established the modern account of Equiano's birthplace.

title: The Works of Mary Wollstonecraft, 7 volumes
author_or_editor: Janet M. Todd and Marilyn Butler (general editors)
reliability_notes: The collected scholarly edition of Wollstonecraft's novels, essays, travels, vindications and juvenilia.

title: Reflections on the Revolution in France
reliability_notes: A student text of Burke's 1790 Reflections with introduction and notes; the Oxford World's Classics series edition.

title: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, 7 volumes (Bury edition)
reliability_notes: The standard annotated edition of Gibbon's history with editorial notes on the sources and the later revisions.

title: The Poems of Ossian and Related Works
reliability_notes: A student edition of Macpherson's poems with the authenticating dissertations and apparatus; reprinted from the early collected editions.

title: Encyclopedia of the Enlightenment
reliability_notes: Signed entries on the philosophers, societies, publications and controversies of the European Enlightenment, including its English and Scottish branches.

title: Essays in the History of Ideas
reliability_notes: Includes the classic studies of primitivism and noble-savage theory and of the eighteenth-century quarrels about taste and romanticism used for this installment's movements.
